NPU engine leaderboard#

One row is one measured run of this engine. A record is only ranked if it names its instrument, its repeat count and its timestamp; see bench/npu-leaderboard/README.md for the shape. Decode latencies are s/token (lower is better, and they are what a user feels); throughputs are tok/s (higher is better). Rows are not comparable across hosts.

No --parallel 8 row is published: at 8 streams the rate is non-stationary inside a run (llama-server's own tg per slot goes 14.99 15.12 14.34 12.10 7.09 6.78 5.70 5.64 as the answers grow, then 14.17 for a fresh batch, with die temp 61-71 C and iGPU sclk 694-2127 MHz swinging normally), so an 8-stream number is a function of where in that decay it is sampled: 112.89 / 1.34x at 06:45Z, 78.87 / 0.97x and 68.29 / 0.92x later the same day.

Measured as the solo arm of the --parallel 2/4 servers (84.33 / 84.22, ten requests) and 81.39 on the --parallel 8 server; across both runs today the same load gave 74.03-88.34, i.e. +-8 %, so compare ratios, not absolute tok/s.

A 2-row decode batch costs 29.0 ms/token per stream against 11.9 ms for one row; with ONEBIT_HRX_DECODE_SPLIT=0 the same server gives 57.59 from a 45 tok/s solo, so the vectorised decode-split path is the suspect -- not settled.
